dedupe_keys.name: erad energy resilience analysis for electric distribution systems

description: ERAD is a free, open-source Python toolkit for assessing how electric distribution assets survive hazards and what that means for energy resilience of the households and critical services they supply. It is developed by the National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, with Kapil Duwadi, Bryan Palmintier, Aadil Latif, Kwami Senam Sedzro and Sherin Ann Abraham as authors, and is described in the Journal of Open Source Software. It represents infrastructure as a connected graph and computes hazard-specific exposure and survival probabilities for poles, lines, cables, transformers, substations, junction boxes, switches and rooftop solar, using fragility curves from the literature for flood, wind, wildfire and earthquake. It supports scenario-based analysis, uncertainty sampling and export of asset-level results, and lets users compare programmes such as undergrounding, microgrids and backup power for critical facilities across neighbourhoods. The README also advertises a Model Context Protocol server with 26 tools. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost, with documentation online and active releases (14 tags, latest commit May 2026). Caveats: fragility curves are generic literature values that may need local calibration. Simulation uses are hazard exposure, fragility-based failure and hardening studies of distribution grids. Related records: model-inl-seismic-contingency-auto-generator covers earthquake contingencies for transmission.
